children: India's BSE Sensex extended early losses to close about 1.1% down at 74,764 on Wednesday, the lowest since June, marking the third session of decreases.
The escalation of tensions between the US and Iran in the Persian Gulf region added to concerns about global energy supplies, pushing oil prices higher and fanning inflation concerns.
Continued foreign fund outflows also weighed on investor sentiment.
Selling pressure was broad-based, led by IT and banks, while metals bucked the broader trend.
HCLTech, Infosys, Tech Mahindra and TCS shed between 2% and 4.6%.
Other laggards included HDFC Bank (-2.2%), ICICI Bank (-0.7%) and Reliance Industries (-1%).
On the upside, Adani Ports outperformed, climbing 3.7%, after winning the bid to develop and operate two dry bulk berths at Paradip Port in Odisha.
Tata Steel (2.4%), Trent (1.1%), NTPC (0.5%) also recorded gains.

title: Sensex Closes at 3-Month Low
